item.stem: A researcher is constructing a confidence interval for a population mean. If the researcher increases the confidence level from 90% to 99%, how will the width of the confidence interval change, and what does this imply about the precision of the estimate?

item.explanation: This item probes the conceptual understanding of the trade-off between confidence level and the width (precision) of the confidence interval. It tests whether students realize that requiring higher confidence (A6) necessarily requires a wider interval, which is inherently less precise, rather than falling for the misconception that higher confidence leads to a better/tighter estimate (B17).
